landability_note: Both findings are backend-only Rust edits confined to a single file, handlers/favorites/mod.rs, with no migration, no schema change, and no client/openapi regen. (1) Fix the error mapping in add_favorite: match on the sqlx error kind (RowNotFound -> ListingNotFound; unique-constraint violation -> AlreadyFavorited) instead of the brittle `.to_string().contains("violates foreign key")` substring test, and make the limit enforcement authoritative at the DB rather than via a non-atomic pre-read. (2) Route is_favorited / get_favorites_count through the repo's existing cheap helpers (is_favorite EXISTS query, count_favorites) instead of loading the full favorites+listings join. Each is verifiable via `cargo build -p reality-server` plus a focused unit/integration test (e.g. add-favorite for a non-existent listing asserts ListingNotFound not a 500). Independently landable by separate implementers.
note: Static analysis only (no compilation, no test execution) per skill. Segment root backend/servers/reality-server/src/ (43 .rs files). This is a mature, heavily-mined segment (85+ historical reality-server findings) and most Rust-expert patterns came up CLEAN this pass (recorded so future rotations don't re-mine): (a) UNWRAP/EXPECT crash paths — every non-test unwrap/expect is either inside a #[cfg(test)] mod (saved_search_alerts.rs:273-305, inquiries.rs:857/969), a guarded invariant (inquiries/mod.rs:274 `cleaned.chars().next().unwrap()` is preceded by an `if cleaned.is_empty() { return false }` guard; extractors/auth.rs:63 `.strip_prefix("portal_session=").unwrap()` is guarded by a `.find(|c| c.trim().starts_with("portal_session="))`), a documented fail-closed rng (handlers/users/mod.rs:558 `.expect("OS rng failed")`), or an intentional fail-fast startup config assertion (state.rs:81-106 JWT_SECRET panics). (b) No `unsafe`, no reachable todo!()/unimplemented!(). (c) services/favorite_alerts.rs is exemplary and already hardened against prior findings (#1999, #1852, #983): per-org RLS context + REPEATABLE READ transactions wrapping enqueue+watermark-advance to close snapshot races. The two findings below are genuine net-new defects in handlers/favorites/mod.rs — a module with NO prior reality-server code-review-finding (grep of backlog.json + all signals/*.json for 'favorites-' / 'favorite-add' returned nothing; existing 'favorite'/'favorites' ids are all in the reality-web segment). Both are grounded in the repo SQL (backend/crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal/searches.rs, portal.rs) and the schema (migration 00063_reality_portal_professional.sql: portal_favorites has UNIQUE(user_id, listing_id) and listing_id FK -> listings).

evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/handlers/favorites/mod.rs:40-74 — FavoritesHandler::add_favorite maps repository errors with a brittle substring test: `if error_str.contains("violates foreign key") { FavoriteResult::ListingNotFound } else { FavoriteResult::DatabaseError(error_str) }`. The DatabaseError arm is surfaced by the POST /favorites route as HTTP 500. Two distinct user-facing cases that SHOULD be 4xx fall through to that 500 arm:

CASE A (deterministic, missing/deleted listing -> 500 instead of 404 ListingNotFound): the backing repo method `RealityPortalRepository::add_favorite` (backend/crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal/searches.rs:416-437) inserts via `INSERT INTO portal_favorites (...) SELECT $1,$2,$3,l.price,l.status FROM listings l WHERE l.id = $2 RETURNING *` and `.fetch_one(...)`. When the listing does not exist the SELECT yields zero rows, so the INSERT inserts nothing and `fetch_one` returns `sqlx::Error::RowNotFound` — NOT a foreign-key violation. `RowNotFound.to_string()` does not contain "violates foreign key", so the handler returns DatabaseError -> HTTP 500. The intended `ListingNotFound` (404) branch is effectively dead code: the listing_id FK (migration 00063_reality_portal_professional.sql:55 `listing_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES listings(id)`) can only fire in the razor-thin window where the listing is deleted between the SELECT and constraint check; the ordinary missing-listing request always 500s.

CASE B (concurrent duplicate -> 500 instead of 409/AlreadyFavorited): portal_favorites has `UNIQUE(user_id, listing_id)` (migration 00063:65). The handler pre-checks duplicates in-memory (`favorites.iter().any(|f| f.listing_id == listing_id)` -> AlreadyFavorited) but this is a non-atomic TOCTOU: two concurrent add_favorite calls for the same (user, listing) can both pass the pre-check, and the second INSERT raises a Postgres unique-constraint violation whose message is "duplicate key value violates unique constraint ..." — again not "violates foreign key" — so it returns DatabaseError -> HTTP 500 rather than the intended AlreadyFavorited. The same TOCTOU affects the limit guard (`favorites.len() >= MAX_FAVORITES_PER_USER` at :54): two concurrent inserts can both pass and push a user past the 100-favorite cap, since nothing enforces the cap at the DB.

Reachability: add_favorite is the handler behind the public authenticated POST favorites route; CASE A is triggered by any request referencing a stale/removed listing id (common for an SEO-indexed public portal where listings expire), CASE B by ordinary double-click / retry races. Net-new: grep of .research/backlog.json and signals/*.json for favorites-add / favorite error-mapping returned nothing (all prior 'favorite(s)' findings are reality-web). Landable backend-only remedy confined to handlers/favorites/mod.rs: match on the concrete sqlx error (RowNotFound -> ListingNotFound, unique-violation via DatabaseError::kind()==UniqueViolation or code 23505 -> AlreadyFavorited) instead of substring-matching to_string(); optionally let the DB be authoritative on duplicates by dropping the in-memory pre-check. Verifiable with `cargo build -p reality-server` + an integration test adding a favorite for a non-existent listing (assert ListingNotFound, not DatabaseError) and a concurrent-duplicate test (assert AlreadyFavorited). Confidence high for CASE A: the INSERT...SELECT RowNotFound path is deterministic and fully traced from handler to repo SQL to schema.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/handlers/favorites/mod.rs — FavoritesHandler::is_favorited (:103-114), get_favorites_count (:145-154), and the add_favorite precondition checks (:48-60) all call `self.repo.get_favorites_with_listings(user_id)` to compute a boolean / a count / a limit comparison. That repo method (searches.rs:440-...) runs a full `portal_favorites JOIN listings` plus a correlated per-row subquery for the cover photo (`(SELECT url FROM listing_photos ... LIMIT 1)`) and materializes every favorite (up to the 100-item cap) with all listing columns — then the handler throws the rows away to return a single bool or a usize length.

The repository already ships purpose-built cheap helpers that the handler ignores: `is_favorite` (searches.rs:535-545) is a single `SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM portal_favorites WHERE user_id=$1 AND listing_id=$2)` whose own doc-comment states it exists to 'avoid fetching the entire favorites collection just to test membership (functional bug at large N where list endpoints cap results)'; and portal.rs provides `count_favorites` (:564, a COUNT query) and `is_favorited` (:574). The handler re-introduces exactly the large-N anti-pattern the repo author documented and guarded against.

Impact: is_favorited is typically called per listing-detail render (the 'is this in my favorites?' heart icon), so every such page load triggers a full favorites+listings join + N photo subqueries instead of one index-only EXISTS. get_favorites_count is similarly O(favorites x listing-columns) for a scalar. This is primarily an efficiency/refactor finding (not a crash), but there is a latent correctness edge too: a count derived from a join DROPS favorites whose listing row was hard-deleted (INNER JOIN), so get_favorites_count and the add_favorite limit pre-check can under-count versus the true portal_favorites row count — using repo count_favorites (COUNT over portal_favorites alone) would be both cheaper and correct.

Net-new: no prior reality-server finding references favorites read amplification (grep of backlog.json + signals/*.json). Landable backend-only remedy confined to handlers/favorites/mod.rs: delegate is_favorited -> repo.is_favorite (EXISTS), get_favorites_count -> repo.count_favorites, and base the add_favorite limit guard on the COUNT rather than the materialized join. Verifiable with `cargo build -p reality-server` + a unit test asserting is_favorited returns correctly without loading the collection. Confidence medium: the handler-to-repo call paths are traced and deterministic; the exact query-plan cost and the hard-delete under-count edge are workload/data-dependent.
